text: {"overall_winner": "A", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Clear thesis statement in opening sentence", "quality": "Explicit position statement", "description": "Essay A directly states its position upfront ('No, driverless cars should not be developed'), making the argument immediately clear to the reader."}, {"evidence": "Three distinct reasons organized in separate paragraphs", "quality": "Organized argument structure", "description": "Essay A presents three main claims (danger, problems, laziness) each developed in its own paragraph, creating a logical progression."}, {"evidence": "Acknowledges counterargument ('Although, having driverless cars sounds pretty cool')", "quality": "Counterargument acknowledgment", "description": "Essay A recognizes the opposing view before refuting it, demonstrating awareness of multiple perspectives."}, {"evidence": "Specific quoted evidence from article integrated into reasoning", "quality": "Evidence integration", "description": "Essay A uses direct quotes ('when the vehicle is in danger of backing into an object') to support its claims about safety features."}, {"evidence": "Logical connection between liability question and business consequences", "quality": "Causal reasoning", "description": "Essay A connects the legal liability problem to concrete consequences (lawsuits, lost business, angry customers) rather than stating problems in isolation."}, {"evidence": "Consistent focus on argument throughout all five paragraphs", "quality": "Sustained argumentation", "description": "Essay A maintains focus on defending its position across the entire essay without losing direction."}]}
